bounded_statement: The selected report's independent-samples t-test result (df=46.0) was computed over a staged row sequence in which every source item's row appears exactly twice (e.g., k1=u01 on two consecutive rows), so each independent unit enters the row-independent procedure twice and the effective sample size is doubled from 12 to 24 per collection.

counterevidence_considered.description: The task explicitly instructs applying the procedure to the complete staged row sequence, so processing the duplicates was authorized instruction-following; this bears on fault attribution but does not negate that the repeated-unit entries are demonstrably present in the computed result.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: Each unit's row appears exactly twice in the staged data; the first duplicated pair shows k1=u01 entered twice with identical measurements, and the pattern repeats through u12/v06.
The task defines k1 and k2 as identifying source items, so a repeated k1 code is the same independent unit entered again, not a new unit.

evidence.description: The workflow passes every staged row, including the duplicate entries, into an independent-samples t-test, a procedure that treats each row value as an independent observation.

source_refs.quoted_text:
staged = rows
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]
result = st.ttest_ind(left, right)

evidence.description: The report's degrees of freedom (46.0 = 24+24-2) confirm that all duplicated entries were counted as independent observations; 12 unique units per collection would yield df=22.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify by hypothesizing that the paired lines are distinct units or distinct repeat measurements that would not constitute the same unit re-entering. This fails: the task defines k1/k2 as unit identifiers, and the duplicated rows carry identical identifiers, so they are the same units by the governing definition; even if read as second measurements, the same unit still enters the row-independent procedure twice. I also checked whether the procedure might account for repetition; ttest_ind has no such mechanism, and df=46.0 confirms all 48 values were counted.

root_cause: The workflow feeds the complete staged sequence, containing an exact second entry for every unit identifier, into scipy.stats.ttest_ind, which treats each row as an independent observation; the duplicated entries of the same k1/k2 source items are therefore counted as additional independent observations, inflating degrees of freedom from 22 to 46.
